messages:
maria: heads-up — saw a regression in the autotuner for long sequences (>1024). it started picking the matmul_conv32 kernel even when throughput was worse after kv cache warmups. attaching quick profile summary.

sunil: ugh. is it reproducible on a fixed machine or noisy? any telemetry lines?

maria: repro is consistent on rtx-a100-80gb and gfx90a. noisy across tenant workloads but reproducible in our perf harness. sample telemetry event: 

```
telemetry: {"event":"kernel_pick","chosen":"matmul_conv32","candidates":["matmul_conv32","gemm_v2","conv_fused_wn"],"reason":["latency_sample","kv_hit_high"],"seq_len":1500,"seq_len_bucket":">1024","kv_hit_rate":0.84,"arch":"gfx90a","avg_latency_ms":3.9,"sample_count":12,"env":"REDWOOD_TUNER=arch-aware,INFER_PICK_DEBUG=1"}
```

maria: note the reason contains kv_hit_high which caused the tuner to prefer a lower-latency path measured at cold-start, but after prefix/KV warmup the effective memory layout pushes matmul_conv32 into a cache-unfriendly regime — measured tail latency increases.

deploy-bot: deploy 1949998899 started by kevin in canary, status: in-progress :rocket:

kevin: can run the canary with extra debug flags. suggested command: 

```
INFER_TRACE=1 REDWOOD_PICK_DEBUG=1 REDWOOD_PICK_HYSTERESIS=8 ./bin/infer --model prod-v2 --backend cuda --seq-len 1500
```

anika: hmm, maybe our telemetry is missing the seqlen bucket and kv_cache_warm flag. propose adding fields: seq_len_bucket, kv_cache_state (cold|warming|warm), pick_stability_ms, and sample_latency_hist (p50,p95). that'll help autotuner avoid flip-flopping.

sunil: agreed. another issue: tuner uses avg_latency over N samples; with KV warmup the distribution is bimodal. averaging hides the tail. we should track weighted tail or p95 and prefer kernels with smaller p95 when p95 delta > pick_stability_ms.

maria: test note: when I force kv_cache_state=warm in the runtime probe, the tuner picked gemm_v2 and tail improved by ~18% (p95 down from 12.4ms to 10.2ms). logs: 

```
[profiling] seq_len=1500 kv_hit_rate=0.92 chosen=gemm_v2 avg=3.2 p95=10.2 sample_count=20 arch=gfx90a
[profiling] seq_len=1500 kv_hit_rate=0.92 chosen=matmul_conv32 avg=3.9 p95=12.4 sample_count=20 arch=gfx90a
```

kevin: proposal for telemetry + knobs: 
- add seq_len_bucket (e.g., <=128, 129-512, 513-1024, >1024)
- kv_cache_state: cold|warming|warm
- pick_metric: p95|avg (default p95 for >1024)
- REDWOOD_PICK_HYSTERESIS (ms) to require candidate p95 improvement > hysteresis to switch

anika: will submit a small PR to emit seq_len_bucket and kv_cache_state from the runtime probe. also will add a debug env REDWOOD_TUNER_SIMULATE_WARM=1 to let tuner run simulated warm traces in CI.

sunil: for autotuner algorithm change, consider: use exponential moving percentile on latency rather than simple avg, and add a sample_count floor (min_samples=8) before switching. also cap oscillation by requiring stable pick for 2 consecutive evaluation windows.

maria: thanks — if you push the telemetry PR and the canary with REDWOOD_PICK_HYSTERESIS=8 I can run the harness and post numbers. current regression is small but customer-visible (p95 up ~15% for some chat workloads).

kevin: starting canary now with flags. will post results in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: canary 1949998899 update: nodes healthy, traces enabled.

maria: adding an extra note — KV cache eviction patterns (when batching mixes short and long sessions) exacerbate the problem. we should include batch composition (frac_long_requests) in telemetry too.

anika: ack — adding frac_long_requests to telemetry schema and a follow-up test to vary batch mixes.

sunil: if the canary looks good, we can land hysteresis default of 8ms and bump pick_metric to p95 for seq_len_bucket ">1024". otherwise revert and iterate.

maria: copied perf harness outputs to the ticket: https://redwood/issue/INF-4312. thanks all.
